title: EDA
text:
This document will include exploratory data analysis of the water potability data set
library(tidyverse)
library(knitr)
library(gt)
source("helpers.R")

title: EDA
text:
1. Description of Dataset
The dataset for this analysis contains water quality metrics for 3276 different water bodies.
There are nine (9) numerical explanatory variables and one (1) categorical response variable (Potability). The variables and their descriptions are as follows:









Variable
Type
Description
Units




ph
Numerical
pH of water, 0 to 14 scale
unitless


Hardness
Numerical
Capacity to precipitate soap
mg/L


Solids
Numerical
Total dissolved solids
ppm


Chloramines
Numerical
Chloramine concentration
ppm


Sulfate
Numerical
Dissolved sulfates
mg/L


Conductivity
Numerical
Electrical conductivity
μS/cm


Organic_carbon
Numerical
Total organic carbon
ppm


Trihalomethanes
Numerical
Trihalomethane concentration
μg/L


Turbidity
Numerical
Suspended solids, measured by light-emission
NTU


Potability
Categorical
Safe for consumption, 1 = potable, 0 = not potable
unitless



Further details and the raw data are available here: https://www.kaggle.com/datasets/adityakadiwal/water-potability
For our analysis, Potability is the response variable while the others are designated as predictors.

text:
2. Data Cleaning

Read in the data


water_data <- read_csv("Data/water_potability.csv")

Rows: 3276 Columns: 10

Check for any NA values


enframe(colSums(is.na(water_data)), # tally the NA values
        name = "Variable", # rename column
        value = "NA Count") |> # rename column
  kable() # nice table format

It looks like we have quite a few NA values. Lets look at how many observations are complete.

sum(complete.cases(water_data))

[1] 2011


Before removing the incomplete observations, let’s confirm that the rate of potability among complete observations is similar to the rate among incomplete observations

water_data |>
  mutate(status = if_else(complete.cases(water_data), "complete", "incomplete")) |> # assign complete/incomplete status
  group_by(status) |> # grup by incomplete/complete
  summarise(n = n(), potability_rate = mean(Potability)) # for each group, report count and mean Potability

# A tibble: 2 × 3
  status         n potability_rate
  <chr>      <int>           <dbl>
1 complete    2011           0.403
2 incomplete  1265           0.369


Potability rates are similar among complete and incomplete observations (40.3% vs 36.9%), indicating that the missing values are not strongly associated with the response. Therefore we will treat the missing values as approximately random and remove these observations. The remaining dataset of complete observations is sufficiently large (n = 2011) to fit models.

water_data <- drop_na(water_data) # removing all observations with NA


Convert Potability to Factor


water_data <- water_data |>
  mutate(Potability = factor(Potability))
